title: Atlas: incident notes & internal comms draft (scratchpad)
content:
Quick context:
Atlas (enterprise customer) reported increased 5xx rate on hosted API starting ~2025-11-19 17:30 PST. Customer noticed timeouts in production and a spike in client retries; their app briefly fell back to cached responses. They opened a support window and asked for a timeline + root-cause.

Goals for this note:
- Capture timeline of events and commands tried (for postmortem)
- Draft an internal status/comm message we can send to Atlas once we have RCA
- Track hypotheses and actions taken (so SRE and CS know who did what)

Observed symptoms (from customer and our telemetry):
- 5xx rate for atlas-org-id climbed from ~0.4% -> 6.2% between 2025-11-19 17:30 and 18:45 PST.
- Per-route latency up by ~450ms p50 for /v1/generate (they use hosted-api model: rwd-gen-2.1)
- Error signature seen in logs: repetitive "rpc error: code = ResourceExhausted desc = KV cache miss overflow" and occasional "cuda runtime error: out of memory" on a small subset of backends.
- KV-cache hit ratio for the tenant dropped from 92% -> 6% during the window.
- Rolling deploy of runtime:release-2025.11.19 happened at 17:10 PST (internal deploy window).

Timeline (rough):
- 2025-11-19 17:10 PST: release-2025.11.19 rollout started (models + runtime kernels).
- 2025-11-19 17:28 PST: first customer complaint (Atlas) via support form.
- 2025-11-19 17:31 PST: automated SLO alert (5xx rate).
- 2025-11-19 17:35 PST: triage started (SRE on-call: Marta Ruiz).
- 2025-11-19 17:45 PST: identified KV cache miss spike and OOM traces in subset of GPU workers.
- 2025-11-19 18:00 PST: attempted mitigation: pin tenant traffic to older model variant rwd-gen-2.0 via routing policy. Partial relief observed.
- 2025-11-19 18:30 PST: rolled back runtime to previous build on 60% of GA pool. Errors subsided but intermittent bursts continued for ~20 minutes.
- 2025-11-19 19:05 PST: customer confirmed degraded experience still present for edge requests; reopened support call.

Commands and artifacts collected (for debugging):
- k logs (example):
  kubectl -n inference logs backend-worker-xyz -c runtime --since=2h | grep -i "ResourceExhausted"
  --- returned repeated lines: "rpc error: code = ResourceExhausted desc = KV cache miss overflow: entries=32412 capacity=32768"

- runtime debug dump:
  curl -sS -H "Authorization: Bearer REDACTED" https://internal-api/redwood/runtime/debug/kvcache?node=backend-worker-xyz | jq .summary
  --- showed kvcache.size=32412, kvcache.capacity=32768, eviction_rate spiking to 18/sec

- GPU OOM snippet (stderr tail):
  [2025-11-19 17:40:12] runtime.cu: kernel_launch failed: CUDA_ERROR_OUT_OF_MEMORY (device 0)
  stack: runtime::serve_loop -> decoder_step -> cudakernel_launcher

- Proxy logs showing client retries:
  WARN proxy: upstream returned 502 after 3 retries for tenant atlas-org-id route /v1/generate

Hypotheses (ranked):
1) KV cache sizing regression in release-2025.11.19 increased per-tenant cache churn for long-tail prefixes; TTL/eviction heuristics changed -> high miss rate -> extra token recomputation -> memory pressure -> OOM in some workers. (Most likely)
2) New kernel selection logic in runtime picks higher-memory kernels for certain sequence lengths, combined with a pathological sequence distribution from Atlas -> OOM on some smaller GPU instances.
3) Networking flakiness causing broken streaming connections -> retries -> burst load -> resource exhaustion (less likely based on metrics).

Quick repro steps (local):
- Recreate long prefix stream: use trace file from Atlas (s3://redwood-debug/atlas/2025-11-19/trace-1.json).
- Run with release-2025.11.19 runtime image locally on a small g4dn-like instance and observe cache eviction rate.
- Scripts used: tools/repro/atlas_replay.sh --tenant atlas-org-id --trace trace-1.json --concurrency 16

Mitigations we tried (and results):
- Pin routing to rwd-gen-2.0 (older model variant) -> partial reduction in errors within 10m.
- Rollback runtime -> errors largely subsided when 60% of GA pool was rolled back; full rollback not done because of other customers and risk.
- Increased kvcache.capacity transiently on affected nodes (manual flag) -> immediate lowering of eviction_rate but not a full fix (because eviction policy still changed behavior).
- Throttle back aggressive client-headers for Atlas via per-tenant QPS cap -> smoothed bursts but not ideal long term.

Open questions / TODOs:
- Exact code diff that caused kvcache eviction heuristic change: PR? (Marta to check runtime PR history around 2025-11-19)
- Are there any model-level config changes in rwd-gen-2.1 that would increase per-request memory (e.g., kv-cache per-layer prefetch)? (Ethan to check model onboarding notes)
- Should we perform full rollback of release-2025.11.19 until a patched fix is available? Risk: other customers might need new kernel fixes contained in this release. (Decision pending)
- Need sanitized trace and customer permission to attach traces to postmortem. (CS owns)

Draft internal status (to paste into #cs-atlas and INF-2345):
---
Short update (internal):
We saw a spike in 5xxs for Atlas starting 2025-11-19 ~17:30 PST correlated with the rollout of release-2025.11.19. Early indicators point to a change in KV cache eviction behavior that increased miss rates for long-tail prefixes, producing extra recompute and memory pressure on a subset of GPU workers which led to OOMs and 5xxs.
Actions taken: routing pinned to older model variant, partial rollback of runtime, temporary increase in kvcache capacity, and QPS throttling for customer to reduce burst load.
Next steps: identify the PR that changed eviction heuristics, patch and validate on staging, coordinate with product on rollback window if required, and prepare RCA for Atlas.
---

Draft external message to Atlas (short, empathetic, non-technical):
Hi Sam and team,
Thanks again for flagging the degraded behaviour — really sorry for the disruption. We briefly investigated and found a regression introduced during a recent internal rollout that temporarily increased processing for some requests. We have taken steps to reduce your error rate (pinned the model variant and applied a partial rollback) and continue to monitor. We'll follow up with a full root-cause analysis and ETA for a permanent fix by EOD tomorrow.
If you'd like an interim call, we can jump on 30 minutes to walk through what we changed.
Thanks,
Alex (on behalf of Redwood SRE/CS)

Owners / playbook assignments (quick):
- Marta R. (SRE): find runtime PR, confirm revert/patch and assemble test case.
- Ethan W. (Applied ML): check model variant differences for rwd-gen-2.1 -> memory footprint.
- Priya S. (CS): coordinate Atlas permission for traces, send short external update.
- Alex C. (me): synthesize postmortem skeleton, ensure linked artifacts are attached.

Notes to self / scratch lines:
- Check telemetry for other tenants with similar long-tail prefix distributions (query: metrics.5xx_rate{kv_miss_rate>0.1})
- Investigate whether kvcache eviction change was intentional (was it in docs? release notes?).
- Add automated regression test that replays long-tail Atlas trace across candidate kernel choices.

Appendix: raw error snippets (sanitized)
1) rpc line: "rpc error: code = ResourceExhausted desc = KV cache miss overflow: entries=32412 capacity=32768"
2) OOM: "CUDA_ERROR_OUT_OF_MEMORY device 0 size 2147483648 requested"
3) proxy: "upstream returned 502 after 3 retries for tenant atlas-org-id"

End of scratchpad.
(Will move to shared DR after RCA draft is ready.)
